extracted.intended_audience: NLP researchers and practitioners developing and evaluating creative-plot generation systems (story-generation researchers, model builders, evaluation engineers)
extracted.subtask_description: Premise-conditioned movie-plot generation and its evaluation: producing long-form narrative plots from premises and assessing them across multiple narrative quality dimensions using reward models, agentic evaluators, and preference-based alignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative Coherence (NQD)
rubrics_metrics.description: Field definition (Positive Focus): Narrative clarity, logical plot progression, coherent world-building, strong cause–effect relationships, and well-integrated subplots. Field definition (Negative Focus): Confusing storytelling, plot holes, inconsistent world-building, disconnected subplots, or illogical character decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used both as a reward-model prompt and as an NQD. Strict output rules for reward-model prompts: (1) Output only a valid JSON object; (2) Include only Narrative_Coherence; (3) Integer value from 0 to 10; (4) For positive prompts: score generously; for negative prompts: 0 = no issues, 10 = severe issues. In agentic evaluation this aspect is further broken down into a 10-criteria 0–1-per-criterion framework (see Agentic Evaluation: Narrative Coherence entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional Turning Points (NQD)
rubrics_metrics.description: Field definition (Positive Focus): Powerful emotional moments, effective turning points, meaningful revelations, and emotionally satisfying narrative shifts. Field definition (Negative Focus): Flat emotional arcs, forced turning points, unearned twists, or moments that fail to engage the audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict output rules for reward-model prompts: (1) Output only JSON; (2) Include only Emotions_Turning_Points; (3) Integer 0–10; (4) Positive prompts: score generously; negative prompts: 0 = no issues, 10 = severe issues. Agentic evaluation uses a 10-criteria rubric focused on conflict, transformation, satisfaction, causality, and audience alignment (see Agentic Evaluation: Emotional Turning Point entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone Consistency (NQD)
rubrics_metrics.description: Field definition (Positive Focus): Successful maintenance of mood, atmosphere, and stylistic coherence throughout the story. Effective emotional consistency, well-maintained genre conventions, and smooth transitions between story beats; intentional tonal shifts are rewarded when they serve narrative purpose. Field definition (Negative Focus): Jarring mood shifts, inconsistent atmosphere, conflicting stylistic elements, genre incoherence, or awkward tonal transitions that disrupt immersion or emotional continuity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict output rules for reward-model prompts: (1) Output only a valid JSON object; (2) Include only Tone_Consistency; (3) Integer 0–10; (4) Score generously for positives; negative prompts: 0 = no issues, 10 = severe issues. Agentic evaluation provides a 10-criterion tonal rubric (see Agentic Evaluation: Tone Consistency).

rubrics_metrics.name: Character Development (NQD)
rubrics_metrics.description: Field definition (Positive Focus): Compelling character arcs, meaningful growth, clear motivations, well-developed relationships, authentic character voices, and satisfying character journeys; emphasis on characters who evolve, learn, or change meaningfully. Field definition (Negative Focus): Weak or static character arcs, lack of growth, unclear motivations, poorly developed relationships, inconsistent character voices, or unsatisfying character journeys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict output rules for reward-model prompts: (1) Output only a valid JSON object; (2) Include only Character_Development; (3) Integer 0–10; (4) Score generously for positives; negative prompts: 0 = no issues, 10 = severe issues. Agentic evaluation uses a 10-criterion character-development framework (see Agentic Evaluation: Character Development).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pacing (NQD)
rubrics_metrics.description: Field definition (Positive Focus): Effective narrative rhythm, well-balanced scene progression, appropriate timing of plot events, and smooth transitions that maintain momentum and audience engagement; pacing should support tension, emotional beats, and story clarity. Field definition (Negative Focus): Uneven or inconsistent pacing, excessive slowdowns or rushed segments, poorly timed plot events, unnecessary filler scenes, or abrupt transitions that disrupt narrative flow or emotional impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict output rules for reward-model prompts: (1) Output only a valid JSON object; (2) Include only Pacing; (3) Integer 0–10; (4) Score generously for positives; negative prompts: 0 = no issues, 10 = severe issues. Agentic evaluation defines 10 pacing sub-criteria to be scored and summed to 10 (see Agentic Evaluation: Pacing Analysis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agentic Evaluation: Narrative Coherence (10-criterion framework)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate a movie plot’s narrative structure and logical consistency using a 10-criteria framework; each criterion scored 0–1 (increments of 0.1 allowed), summed for a total out of 10.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoring criteria (total 10 points): Plot Progression; Causal Connectivity; Plot Integrity (no plot holes/contradictions); Conflict Focus (sustained central conflict); Protagonist Consistency / Authenticity; Supporting Character Function; Resolution; Pacing Appropriateness; Thematic Integration; Tonal Consistency. Output format: list each subcriterion as X.X and TOTAL: X.X/10. This prompt enforces precise numeric scoring and structured output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agentic Evaluation: Emotional Turning Point (10-criterion framework)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and evaluate the primary emotional turning point using a 10-criteria framework focused on emotional impact and character change; each criterion scored and summed to 10.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoring criteria (total 10 points, organized across conceptual groups): (Conflict & Character Foundation - 4 points): Conflict Resolution, Character Believability, Character Transformation; (Narrative Construction - 3 points): Emotional Satisfaction, Narrative Causality; (Technical & Structural Elements - 3 points): Thematic Crystallization, Relationship Impact, Cinematic Execution, Structural Necessity, Audience Alignment. Output lists each subcriterion and TOTAL: X.X/10. The framework emphasizes whether the turning point addresses the central conflict, yields believable transformation, and provides emotionally satisfying payoffs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agentic Evaluation: Character Development (10-criterion framework)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate protagonist character development using a 10-criteria framework assessing motivation, arc progression, psychological depth, and narrative function; scores summed to 10.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoring criteria (total 10 points): Core Character Elements (4 points): Motivation Clarity, Behavioral Consistency, Character Arc (believable transformation), Psychological Depth; Character Foundation (3 points): Backstory Integration, Audience Connection, Character Distinctiveness; Narrative Function (3 points): Relationship Dynamics, Plot Agency, Thematic Alignment. Output lists each subcriterion and TOTAL: X.X/10. Emphasizes clear goals, consistent actions, believable growth, and integration into plot/thematic structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agentic Evaluation: Pacing Analysis (10-criterion framework)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess narrative pacing using a 10-criteria framework measuring rhythm, momentum, and emotional timing; each subcriterion scored 0–1 and summed to 10.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoring criteria (10 items): Premise Establishment Speed; Structural Foundation; Pacing Consistency; Event Frequency; Scene Purposefulness; Tension Management; Transition Quality; Emotional Beat Timing; Climax Timing; Genre–Tone Alignment. Output format enumerates each item X.X and TOTAL: X.X/10. Emphasizes both macro (structure, climax) and micro (beat timing, transitions) temporal qualities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agentic Evaluation: Tone Consistency (10-criterion framework)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate tonal coherence with a 10-criteria framework assessing atmosphere, stylistic unity, and emotional continuity; scores summed to 10.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoring criteria (10 items): Initial Atmosphere Establishment; Scene-to-Scene Consistency; Tonal Relief Integration; Earned Tone Shifts; Dialogue Style Consistency; Visual Reinforcement; Stakes Alignment; Comedy/Drama Balance; Ending Consistency; Motif and Symbol Unity. Output enumerates each subcriterion and TOTAL: X.X/10. Rewards maintained mood and justified tonal shifts; penalizes jarring or inconsistent tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Positive–Negative Aspect Rating Ensemble (reward construction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensemble method to synthesize aspect-level reward scores: each ensemble model m outputs a positive score r+_{a,m}(p) and a negative score r−_{a,m}(p) per aspect; aggregate aspect rating computed as r_a(p) = sum_m (r+_{a,m}(p) − r−_{a,m}(p)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: mitigate individual model bias via model diversity. Implementation notes: ensemble includes Qwen-2.5-7B, Llama-3.2-70B, Llama-3.1-8B, DeepSeek-14B, Gemma-27B; Gemma-27B additionally generates premise descriptions from movie plots for DPO dataset curation. Aggregation produces continuous aspect-level rewards used to train the reward model and DPO pipeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: DPO Candidate Plot Selection Thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria for retaining candidate plots during DPO dataset curation: a candidate is retained as the accepted plot only when it achieves the highest reward score (≥ 8) and outperforms the next-best model by a margin of at least 0.5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a hard acceptance rule used when constructing DPO preference pairs: ensures high-quality positive examples (reward >= 8) and a clear margin over alternatives (>= 0.5). Used with frontier models (GPT-4.1, Claude Sonnet 4, Gemini 2.0 Flash) when selecting candidate plots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental statistical evaluation protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Set of statistical metrics and procedures used to compare generated plots vs. originals and baselines: compute mean scores per aspect, bootstrap-based 95% confidence intervals over paired differences, effect sizes (Cohen’s d), probability that generated plots outperform originals, and Welch’s t-tests for secondary validation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: combine resampling-based estimation (bootstrap CIs, probability of dominance) and parametric testing (Welch’s t-test) to ensure robustness to distributional assumptions while enabling interpretable effect-size comparisons. Report mean differences, 95% CIs, p-values, Cohen's d, and dominance probabilities to characterize both statistical significance and practical magnitude.
